How much does roof replacement cost?

Tearing the old roof off and putting a new one on — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$5,900–$46,000

National average $9,607

Bay Area: $10,239–$22,586 (avg $16,109) — roughly 60–70% above the national average.

Why quotes run $7,500 to $60,000

Material
Asphalt shingles: $7,500–$14,000. Tile or metal: $20,000–$60,000. Material is the single biggest lever on the quote.
Size & shape
Square footage, pitch, dormers, and valleys. Steep or cut-up roofs slow the crew down, and you pay for the hours.
Tear-off & deck
Layers to strip and rotten decking found underneath. Two layers costs more to remove than one; deck repairs get found during the job, not quoted upfront.
Permits & code
Bay Area permits run $500–$2,500, and California’s Title 24 cool-roof rules can dictate which materials you’re allowed to use.
Material tiers

What the money buys

Asphalt shingles
$7,500–$14,000

The default for most homes. Lasts 20–30 years. Cheapest to install and cheapest to repair.

Tile or metal
$20,000–$60,000

Two to four times the upfront cost. Tile lasts 50+ years, metal 40–70. Worth it if you’re staying put.

Bottom line: asphalt wins on price; tile and metal win on lifespan. Selling within 10 years? Asphalt is the rational pick.

Common questions

How long does a roof replacement take?

One to three days for asphalt on most homes. Tile and metal take longer — up to a week or more on steep or complex roofs.

How long does a new roof last?

Asphalt shingles: 20–30 years. Metal: 40–70 years. Tile: 50 years or more. Ventilation and installation quality matter as much as the material.

Should I repair or replace?

Replace when the roof is past 20 years (asphalt), leaks in multiple spots, or the deck sags. Repair when the damage is isolated — a few lifted shingles, one bad flashing — and the roof is otherwise young.

Do I need a permit?

Almost always, and especially in the Bay Area — San Francisco permits run $500–$2,500. A reputable roofer pulls the permit for you. If they ask you to do it, that’s a red flag.

Every roof prices differently.

The range above is a national average. Your price depends on material, size, pitch, and local labor rates. Take a photo of your roof in Brightglow for an estimate on the actual roof, and to compare local roofers who’ve done the same work.
